players.product: T-Head in-house silicon (CPUs, Zhenwu AI processors incl. Zhenwu M890, networking chips) deployed in Alibaba Cloud data centers

quarterly_data.signal: Alibaba's June quarter 2026 results release: starting this quarter, Cloud Intelligence Group and T-Head were combined to form a new AI Cloud and Compute Services segment. Its revenue was RMB48,437 million (US$7,139 million), an increase of 45% from RMB33,418 million in the same quarter of 2025, primarily driven by public cloud revenue growth including the increasing adoption of AI-related products (the release says total and external-customer revenue growth both accelerated to 45%); segment adjusted EBITA increased by 133% to RMB5,628 million (US$830 million) from RMB2,419 million. The release adds that T-Head's proprietary silicon also spans storage chips, and that the Zhenwu chips' external customers on Alibaba Cloud span over 20 industries, including autonomous driving, Internet and financial services.
quarterly_data.figure: AI Cloud and Compute Services revenue RMB48,437 million (+45% vs RMB33,418 million); segment adjusted EBITA RMB5,628 million (+133% vs RMB2,419 million); Zhenwu external customers across over 20 industries

quarterly_data.signal: Alibaba's June quarter 2026 results release: capital expenditures (RMB67,678 million) were an increase of 75% compared to RMB38,676 million in the same quarter of 2025. Free cash flow was an outflow of RMB44,670 million (US$6,584 million), compared to an outflow of RMB18,815 million a year earlier, mainly attributed to the increase in cloud infrastructure expenditure.
quarterly_data.figure: capex +75% YoY (vs RMB38,676 million); free cash flow outflow RMB44,670 million (vs outflow RMB18,815 million)

quarterly_data.signal: Alibaba's June quarter 2026 results release: the new AI Labs and Applications segment (AI model labs, Qwen Consumer Business Group and QwenWork) had revenue of RMB3,338 million (US$492 million), an increase of 16% from RMB2,882 million; its adjusted EBITA loss compares with a loss of RMB3,224 million in the same quarter of 2025, primarily due to increased investment in AI capabilities and higher inference cost related to the Qwen app. The company says 250 million users have had their first AI-driven shopping experience through the Qwen app's agentic features since the app's launch.
quarterly_data.figure: AI Labs and Applications revenue RMB3,338 million (+16% vs RMB2,882 million); year-ago adjusted EBITA loss RMB3,224 million; 250 million users

quarterly_data.signal: Alibaba's June quarter 2026 results release: China E-commerce revenue was RMB110,900 million, a decrease of 8%, with customer management revenue down 7% year-over-year (up 1% on a like-for-like basis excluding the contra revenue impact of the new business development program), a slow-down the company attributes primarily to weaker transaction activities; International E-commerce revenue was RMB27,761 million (a decrease of 1%) and AliExpress achieved operating profit; Global Wholesale revenue was RMB13,906 million (an increase of 7%). 88VIP members increased by double digits year-over-year to approximately 64 million as of June 30, 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: China E-commerce RMB110,900 million (-8%); International E-commerce RMB27,761 million (-1%); Global Wholesale RMB13,906 million (+7%); 88VIP approximately 64 million

quarterly_data.signal: Alibaba's June quarter 2026 results release: income from operations was RMB15,161 million (US$2,234 million), a decrease of 57%, primarily due to the decrease in adjusted EBITA, an impairment of goodwill of RMB4,458 million (US$657 million) relating to businesses in All others, and a provision in relation to the fine of EUR550 million imposed by the European Commission under the Digital Services Act.
quarterly_data.figure: income from operations RMB15,161 million (-57%); goodwill impairment RMB4,458 million; EUR550 million Digital Services Act fine provision
